meta.title: Fed Signal Tracker
meta.description: Curated FOMC meeting log cross-referencing statement language shifts with rate outcomes and Treasury-market reactions.
meta.author: Christopher Givan
meta.methodology: Same-day (2pm statement to 3pm close) yield changes sourced from Treasury.gov H.15 series and cross-checked against Fed statement archive. Stance reflects the statement + SEP composite, not just the decision. This dataset is curated by hand — not an automated feed.
meta.coverage: Selected inflection meetings from the 2022 hiking cycle through the 2026 hold cycle.

meetings.statement_summary: Liftoff after two years at the zero lower bound. Signals an extended tightening path with multiple hikes through year-end.

phrase_changes.phrase: Ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate
Expects to maintain this target range

meetings.notes: Statement delivered as expected but Powell's hawkish press conference pulled the entire curve higher. Dissent from Bullard for +50.

meetings.statement_summary: First 75 bp hike since 1994. Statement pivots from forward-guided hikes to data-dependence as May CPI printed 8.6%.

phrase_changes.phrase: Strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective
Ongoing increases in the target range

meetings.notes: Counterintuitive rally — Powell's line that 75 bp 'would not be common' was read as a ceiling. Market was already priced for 75 via the WSJ leak.

meetings.statement_summary: Delivers fourth consecutive 75 bp hike but introduces 'cumulative tightening' and 'lags' language, flagging a slowdown in pace.

phrase_changes.phrase: Cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity
Determining the pace of future increases

meetings.notes: Statement read dovish on first pass; Powell's presser erased it by flagging a higher terminal rate. Classic pace-vs-destination disconnect.

meetings.statement_summary: Downshifts to 25 bp. Statement replaces 'pace' of future increases with 'extent' — hinting the end of the cycle is in view.

phrase_changes.phrase: Pace of future increases → extent of future increases
Ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate

meetings.notes: Powell's acknowledgment that the 'disinflationary process has started' drove a risk-on rally. Widely cited as the dovish pivot that aged poorly.

meetings.statement_summary: First hold of the cycle paired with a hawkish SEP — median dot moves to 5.6% implying two more hikes. Labeled 'skip' in the press conference.

phrase_changes.phrase: Holding the target range steady at this meeting allows the Committee to assess additional information
Additional policy firming may be appropriate

meetings.notes: Market largely priced the hold; the hawkish dots barely moved terminal rate pricing. The 'skip' framing let the Fed preserve optionality.

meetings.statement_summary: Pivot meeting. Inserts 'any' before 'additional policy firming' and the dot plot pencils in three 25 bp cuts for 2024.

phrase_changes.phrase: Additional policy firming → any additional policy firming
In determining the extent of any additional policy firming

meetings.notes: The 'any' is the highest-signal single word of the cycle. Two-year dropped nearly a basis point per minute for an hour. Powell did not push back on easing financial conditions.

meetings.statement_summary: Holds. SEP retains three cuts for 2024 despite hotter-than-expected Jan/Feb CPI. Powell stresses the bar to re-hike is high.

phrase_changes.phrase: Inflation has eased over the past year but remains elevated
Risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are moving into better balance

meetings.notes: Market feared the dots would drop to two cuts; the 3-cut hold was received as a dovish surprise. Curve bull-steepened.

meetings.statement_summary: First cut of the easing cycle and it's a 50 bp 'insurance' move. Statement reframes mandate language as 'gained greater confidence' on inflation.

phrase_changes.phrase: Gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent
Judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance

meetings.notes: Classic buy-the-rumor, sell-the-news. The front end backed up despite the larger cut because the SEP dots showed only 50 bp more in 2024. Dissent from Bowman for 25 bp.

meetings.statement_summary: Third straight cut paired with a hawkish SEP — 2025 median moved from four cuts to two. Statement adds 'extent and timing' hedge.

phrase_changes.phrase: Additional adjustments → extent and timing of additional adjustments
Carefully assess incoming data

meetings.notes: Hawkish cut. Hammack dissented for a hold. The 'extent and timing' insertion mirrored the 'any' move in Dec 2023 but in reverse — same linguistic tell, opposite direction.

meetings.statement_summary: First 2025 meeting. Holds after three consecutive 2024 cuts. Removes 'made progress toward 2 percent' phrase without adding a replacement — Powell calls it statement shortening, not a signal change.

phrase_changes.phrase: inflation has made progress toward the Committee's 2 percent objective
inflation remains somewhat elevated

meetings.notes: Powell explicitly downplayed the language removal in the press conference — 'shortening the statement, not meant to send a signal.' Market initially sold off, then fully reversed during the presser. End-of-day moves were small (2Y +2 bp, 10Y flat), consistent with the neutral read.

meetings.statement_summary: Adds uncertainty language and announces a large QT slowdown — Treasury redemption cap cut from $25B to $5B/month starting April. Powell flags tariffs as an inflation driver. GDP forecast cut to 1.7% from 2.1%.

phrase_changes.phrase: uncertainty around the economic outlook has increased
Treasury securities redemption cap reduced to $5 billion per month

meetings.notes: Statement stance labeled hawkish on tariff inflation framing, but the yield reaction was dovish — QT slowdown (largest since 2019) and the GDP downgrade brought both 2Y and 10Y down 4–5 bp. Waller dissented, preferring to hold the existing QT pace. The market read the QT cut as more meaningful than the rhetorical hawkishness.

meetings.statement_summary: First explicit dual-mandate tension in the statement: heightened risks of both higher unemployment and higher inflation simultaneously — the Fed's clearest stagflation acknowledgment. Uncertainty language upgraded to 'increased further.'

phrase_changes.phrase: uncertainty about the economic outlook has increased → has increased further
risks to both sides of our dual mandate have risen

meetings.notes: Decision was fully priced; same-day reaction was muted. The 10Y fell 4 bp on the day — the stagflation framing was read as growth-negative enough to bring long rates down despite inflation risk. 2Y flat. Volatile intermeeting period driven by the April tariff shock; the May statement itself was a non-event relative to what had already been priced.

meetings.statement_summary: Slight de-escalation: uncertainty language softens from 'increased further' to 'remains elevated.' Fiscal concerns drove the 10Y notably higher over the intermeeting period per FOMC minutes, but the statement itself was a non-event.

phrase_changes.phrase: uncertainty about the economic outlook has increased further → uncertainty about the economic outlook remains elevated

meetings.notes: The softening of uncertainty language (from 'increased further' to 'remains elevated') was the dovish tell — signaling the peak of the dual-mandate tension framing. Same-day yield reaction was essentially flat. The FOMC minutes attributed the intermeeting 10Y rise to fiscal concerns rather than Fed signaling.

meetings.statement_summary: Holds but two members dissent for a cut — Bowman and Waller, the first simultaneous double dissent since 1993. Statement language acknowledges the first-half growth moderation for the first time.

phrase_changes.phrase: economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace → growth of economic activity moderated in the first half of the year

meetings.notes: Market was surprised the majority held. The hawkish surprise drove a bear flattening — 2Y surged 8 bp as a cut was repriced out of near-term expectations; 10Y rose only 4 bp. The dual dissent (Bowman and Waller) was the strongest leading indicator of an imminent September cut: two dissents for easier policy is the highest-reliability pre-cut signal in the modern FOMC era.

meetings.statement_summary: First cut of the 2025 easing cycle. Statement adds formal labor weakness language — job gains slowed, unemployment edged up — and explicitly flags rising downside employment risks. Miran dissented for -50bp.

phrase_changes.phrase: Job gains have slowed, and the unemployment rate has edged up but remains low
downside risks to employment have risen
Inflation remains somewhat elevated → Inflation has moved up and remains somewhat elevated

meetings.notes: Buy the rumor, sell the news — the cut was fully priced after the July double dissent, so same-day reaction was minimal (2Y +1 bp, 10Y +2 bp). The curious language change on inflation ('has moved up') alongside dovish employment additions created a mixed read. Miran's -50bp dissent signaled internal dovish pressure that would not materialize until the dot plot shifted.

meetings.statement_summary: Cuts -25bp but delivers a hawkish presser surprise — Powell states December cut is 'not a foregone conclusion.' Statement announces QT end date of December 1. December cut probability collapses from ~98% to ~67% post-statement.

phrase_changes.phrase: Committee will conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings on December 1
downside risks to employment rose in recent months (upgraded framing)

meetings.notes: Hawkish cut — Powell's 'not a foregone conclusion' line on December was the headline surprise. Bear flattening: 2Y +9 bp (December cut removed), 10Y +5 bp. Dissents from Miran (-50bp) and Schmid (hold) — the first two-dissent meeting since July, but in opposite directions. QT end announcement was the dovish offset but was overshadowed by the presser guidance.

meetings.statement_summary: Cuts -25bp but dot plot is aggressively hawkish — median 2026 rate revised to 3.4% (one cut) from September's 2.9% (four cuts). Three dissents, most since September 2019. Statement adds reserve adequacy language and announces shorter-term Treasury purchases.

phrase_changes.phrase: reserve balances have declined to ample levels
initiating purchases of shorter-term Treasury securities to maintain adequate reserves

meetings.notes: Dovish cut, hawkish dots — the mirror of December 2023. Front end rallied (2Y −7 bp) despite the hawkish dot plot revision, as Powell emphasized labor weakness as the primary rationale for cutting. Curve steepened +4 bp (bull steepening). Dissents from Miran (-50bp), Goolsbee (hold), and Schmid (hold) — the three-way split reflects genuine internal disagreement about the pace of easing.

meetings.statement_summary: First 2026 meeting. Holds following three 2025 cuts. Labor language improved — 'edged up' replaced with 'stabilization.' Inflation de-escalated: 'has moved up' phrase removed. Balance-sheet language dropped as QT fully ended Dec 1. Two governors (Miran, Waller) dissented for cuts.

phrase_changes.phrase: Job gains have slowed, and the unemployment rate has edged up but remains low → Job gains have remained low, and the unemployment rate has shown some signs of stabilization
Inflation has moved up and remains somewhat elevated → Inflation remains somewhat elevated
reserve balances have declined to ample levels
initiating purchases of shorter-term Treasury securities to maintain adequate reserves

meetings.notes: Soft landing optimism — labor market stabilizing, inflation de-escalating. Statement dropped the Dec QT/balance-sheet language now that those operations are complete. Two dovish dissents (Miran and Waller both preferred cuts) signal internal dovish pressure but majority comfortable pausing. Powell called economy on 'firm footing.' Yields moved modestly higher on the hold.

meetings.statement_summary: Holds. First explicit mention of Middle East geopolitical risk in the statement. Hot PPI data (+0.7% vs 0.3% expected) drove a bear-flattening yield spike on the meeting day. SEP dot plot revised for lower-3% Fed Funds by 2027, but near-term cuts repriced out.

phrase_changes.phrase: The implications of developments in the Middle East for the U.S. economy are uncertain
unemployment rate has shown some signs of stabilization → unemployment rate has been little changed in recent months

meetings.notes: Geopolitical risk entered the statement for the first time in the cycle — energy price pass-through from Middle East conflict driving inflation concerns. Hot PPI print (+0.7%) landed the same day, reinforcing the hawkish read. 2Y spiked 10 bp as near-term cut pricing was removed. SEP dot plot saw Low-3% by 2027 but the 2026 path was revised higher. Only Miran dissented for a cut; the rest of the committee closed ranks around caution.

meetings.statement_summary: Holds with a historic 8-4 dissent split — most since October 1992. Inflation language upgraded to 'is elevated' (dropping 'somewhat') and explicitly cites energy prices. Middle East uncertainty language escalated. Three hawkish dissenters (Hammack, Logan, Kashkari) opposed easing bias; one dovish dissenter (Miran) wanted a cut.

phrase_changes.phrase: Available indicators suggest → Recent indicators suggest
Inflation remains somewhat elevated → Inflation is elevated, in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices
The implications of developments in the Middle East for the U.S. economy are uncertain → Developments in the Middle East are contributing to a high level of uncertainty about the economic outlook
Uncertainty about the economic outlook remains elevated

meetings.notes: The inflation language shift from 'remains somewhat elevated' to 'is elevated…in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices' is the starkest upgrade in the easing cycle — dropping 'somewhat' is a significant escalation. Three members dissented hawkishly against the easing bias ('extent and timing of additional adjustments') while Miran dissented dovishly for a cut — simultaneous both-direction dissents. Powell announced he will remain on the Board after his chair term expires in May, with Warsh's nomination advancing in the Senate. Market reaction was contained (2Y +4 bp, 10Y +2 bp) given the historic split vote.

meetings.statement_summary: Kevin Warsh’s first meeting as Fed Chair. Statement dramatically shortened to ~130 words — shortest since 2007 — stripping all forward guidance, easing bias, and balance-of-risks framing. Statement concludes with the new declaration “This Committee will deliver price stability.” Dot plot flipped from implied cut to implied hike: median 2026 rate rose to 3.8% from 3.4% in March. 17 of 18 officials see upside inflation risks. 2026 PCE forecast raised to 3.6% from 2.7%. Unanimous 12–0 vote.

phrase_changes.phrase: In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate...
The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance
All forward guidance language on future rate path

Inflation is elevated, in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices → Inflation remains elevated relative to the Committee’s 2 percent goal, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy
This Committee will deliver price stability

meetings.notes: Warsh’s inaugural FOMC produced the most hawkish single-meeting shift in the current cycle. Statement cut from ~341 to ~130 words — Warsh called it ‘a bit shorter, a bit simpler’ and said forward guidance is ‘not well suited for the current policy conjuncture.’ Dot plot median for end-2026 rose to 3.8% (above midpoint of 3.625%), signaling a likely +25 bp hike before year-end. PCE inflation forecast raised from 2.7% to 3.6% — starkest single-meeting upgrade since post-COVID. Short end led the sell-off: 2Y +15 bp to 4.21% (largest Fed-day move since March 2008). Long end muted, curve flattened ~10 bp. 10Y approximate — needs H.15 verification.

predictive_phrases.interpretation: Inserting 'any' before a tightening phrase is the Fed's most reliable public tell for an imminent pivot. Historically precedes the end of a hike cycle by 0–1 meetings.

predictive_phrases.phrase: extent and timing of additional adjustments
predictive_phrases.interpretation: Hedging both magnitude and schedule is a stronger slowdown signal than hedging magnitude alone. Coincided with a multi-meeting hold starting Jan 2025.
Confidence language has a short half-life — it shows up in the statement that contains the policy move, not the ones leading up to it.
Flags a pace change, not a direction change. Easy to misread as dovish when it is really a pivot to smaller, longer-duration hikes.
Appears when the Fed wants to reassert its anti-inflation mandate. Usually coincides with an upside policy surprise.
Shifts the conversation from 'how fast' to 'how much more.' Historically signals 1–2 hikes remaining.
Signals that labor-market weakness is now weighted alongside inflation. Precedes easing bias.

predictive_phrases.phrase: determining the pace of future increases
predictive_phrases.interpretation: Often gets headline treatment but does little to move the terminal rate. Better read as cover for the next SEP than as policy guidance.

research_notes.title: The 'any' tell
research_notes.body: The December 2023 insertion of 'any' before 'additional policy firming' is the cleanest single-word signal in the modern statement era. It traveled roughly -30 bp in the 2Y within minutes. The symmetric move in Dec 2024 ('extent and timing') produced the opposite trade with similar magnitude. Single-word edits in the forward-guidance paragraph tend to outperform SEP changes on same-day reaction.

research_notes.title: Statement vs. presser
research_notes.body: Statements are drafted by committee; press conferences are Powell. The Nov 2022 meeting is the textbook case — statement added dovish language ('cumulative tightening, lags') but Powell's presser flagged a higher terminal, flattening the curve 12 bp. The signal lives in both documents and the gap between them matters.

research_notes.title: Buy the rumor, sell the dots
research_notes.body: When markets have fully priced a decision, the reaction runs entirely through the SEP dot plot. Sept 2024 delivered a larger-than-expected cut but the dots showed only 50 more bp in 2024 — the front end sold off despite the dovish action. The dots are the marginal information when the decision itself is priced.

research_notes.title: Data caveat
research_notes.body: This dataset is hand-curated from the Federal Reserve statement archive and Treasury H.15 daily yields. It is not an automated feed. Each entry is verifiable against the FOMC statement and next-day H.15 release. Expansion targets: intraday reaction windows (30-min, 60-min), Fed funds futures repricing, and dissent history visualizations.
